messages.subject: Fulfill publication requirements with ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

I have to produce a simple plot that
should fulfill the requirments of plots for that specific journal,
which are:

"Figures should not normally exceed 8.5 cm wide (single column) or 17.5 cm by 22.5 cm (double column) when printed. The dimensions of figures submitted for scanning must not exceed 20 by 25 cm. Lettering should be in ´sans-serif´ type (Helvetica is preferred) with only the first letter of the first word and of any proper names capitalised. The x-height after reduction should be 1.3-1.7 mm (or 8-10 point in Helvetica). Thus for the reduction of graphs to 30, 40 or 50% of original linear dimensions, the initial x-height of lettering would be 5, 4 or 3 mm (c. 30, 22 and 18 pt) respectively. Proportionately smaller sizes of type, symbols, grid marks and curve thickness should be used for lesser reductions. Symbols and grid marks should be the same respective sizes and, after reduction, curves and axes should not exceed 1.5 pt in thickness unless required for clarity. Lines should not be thinner than 0.5 pt, or they may drop out during printing."

So there are some points which are easy like the sans-serif font.
With ggsave I can set the appropriate width for the plot (e.g. 8.5 cm for single column) but what is the default font size in ggplot2 resp. how can I- set it to 8-10 points (1.3-1.7 mm x-height). How can I ensure that all lines are between 0.5 and 1.5 pt when saved as pdf with a given widht/height?

Thank you for your help,

Best regards,
Johannes

--

messages.author: 6e0a397d1d4aab5b
messages.subject: Re: Fulfill publication requirements with ggplot2
parts:
Dear (servus) Johannes,

I'm sure Babtiste, Koshke, Brandon, Hadley and the other experts can
give you better advice but for a start I can give you an example of
one of my graphs since I face exactly the same problems. This is how I
think I solved these problems:

rm(list=ls())

library(proto)
library(grid)
library(reshape)
library(plyr)
library(digest)
library(ggplot2)
library(tools)

setwd("C:\\Users\\mhk\\Documents\\nur.fueR\\ggsave\\")

df.perc.2 <- structure(list(trt = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L),
class = "factor", .Label = c("0-1", "1-2", "2-3")),
resp = c(100, 94.0193416337148, 90.4454585871723,
100, 97.865467535666, 95.8563947267053),
group = structure(c(2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("eggs in
worker cells", "eggs in drone cells"), class = "factor"),
se = c(0, 1.68994661360938, 2.95728999211006,
0, 0.549126551165786, 0.824844616926236)),
.Names = c("trt", "resp", "group", "se"), row.names = c(NA, -6L),
class = "data.frame")

ggplot(df.perc.2, aes(y = resp, x = trt, group = group, colour =
group, linetype = group)) +
scale_colour_manual(values = c("#000000", "#000000")) +
geom_smooth(aes(ymax = resp + se, ymin = resp - se), data = df.perc.
2, stat = "identity", size = 0.5) +
opts(legend.position = c(0.3803, 0.31), legend.background =
theme_rect(colour = 0)) +
opts(legend.key = theme_rect(colour = 0)) +
opts(legend.key.size = unit(c(0.9, 0.9), "lines")) +
opts(legend.title = theme_blank()) +
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 9)) +
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour = "white", size = 0.5)) +
scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0.05), name = "age range of eggs
[day]") +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.02, 0), breaks = seq(90, 100, 5),
name = "eggs remaining [%]") +
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 9, vjust = 0.9),
axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.9)) +
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 11, vjust = 0.61, hjust = 0.6),
axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.555, vjust = 0.59,
angle = 90)) +
opts(plot.margin = unit(c(0.3, 0.3, -0.03, -0.23), "lines"))

ggsave("A.plot7.pdf", width = 85/25.4, height = 85/25.4, family =
"sans")

In "geom_smooth" I have added "size = 0.5". In "opts(axis.title.y =
theme_text(.." I have set the size to 11. "opts(plot.margin)", but I'm
sure you use this as well, is extremely useful to make the most out of
a given space. And in the ggsave command you can set the width, hight
and font type.

This graph was produced with the old version of ggplot2. I hope it is
compatible with the new version. Comming back to your questions: I
would always set the font size manually. In this way you know what you
have. I hope the font size I set in the code is the font size in the
PDF. If not this would be a disaster, you're right. I'm curious hear
from the ggplot2 experts about this problem.

On a slightly different note, Hadley and others, would it be possible
in the future to set R in a way that the window presenting the graph
is identical to the PDF? This would save a lot of work and time when
creating a graph. I'm not sure how to do that but (fortunately ;-) I'm
not an expert because I guess this wold be a lot of work.

Best wishes and I hope the example above was useful to you,

Martin

p.s.: Ich bin ebenfalls Österreicher, genauer gesagt Grazer. Wo in
Österreich arbeiten Sie? Es gibt meines Wissens noch nicht viele
Österreicher, die ggplot2 verwenden.
